chose: The on-demand unit gets its envctl the way `make up` always did: ExecStartPre builds it as the checkout's owner (runuser -u <user> -- bash -c 'HOME=~<user> exec make -s envctl', cargo through `nix develop .#rust`), and ExecStart, as root, runs <checkout>/target/debug/envctl deploy --on-demand.
options: build as the owner in the checkout (ExecStartPre), run that binary as root
package envctl as a flake output (rustPlatform.buildRustPackage) and put it on the unit's path from the nix store
run the whole unit's make, envctl included, as the owner, with root only for docker and STORAGE (needs C83's second option)
gray: Root runs a binary the owner's user built from the owner's checkout. Before, root ran deploy.py from the same checkout, which is the same trust, and `make -s up`, which built envctl as the owner, already ran inside it. A store-built envctl would pin the deploy to the flake input dotfiles locks rather than the checkout, which changes what `git pull` on home deploys. No convention covers it. The owner chose Rust and envctl; this call is only how the unit gets that binary.
